title: Extra Time
desc: Banned techniques, statistical anomalies & the matches nobody expected

questions.q: The 'Fosbury Flop' revolutionised the high jump. Before Dick Fosbury, what technique did most athletes use?
questions.a: The straddle (or 'Western Roll') — going over face-down. Fosbury went over backwards at the 1968 Olympics and won gold

questions.q: In cricket, only one player has scored 400 runs in a single Test innings. Who?
questions.a: Brian Lara — 400 not out for the West Indies vs England in 2004

questions.q: The 'Miracle on Ice' refers to which specific match, between which teams, in which year?
questions.a: USA vs USSR in ice hockey at the 1980 Winter Olympics in Lake Placid — the amateur US team beat the dominant Soviet professionals

questions.q: Why was the underarm bowling incident in 1981 between Australia and New Zealand so controversial?
questions.a: Australia's captain instructed his bowler to roll the ball along the ground for the last delivery, making it impossible for NZ to hit a six to tie — legal but considered deeply unsportsmanlike

questions.q: In boxing, the 'phantom punch' that knocked out Sonny Liston was thrown by whom, and why is it controversial?
questions.a: Muhammad Ali in 1965 — many ringside observers couldn't see the punch connect, leading to conspiracy theories that the fight was fixed

questions.q: What is 'Moneyball' and which baseball team pioneered the approach?
questions.a: Using statistical analysis (sabermetrics) instead of traditional scouting — pioneered by the Oakland Athletics under GM Billy Beane in the early 2000s

questions.q: Leicester City won the 2015-16 Premier League at odds of 5000-1. What had they nearly done the season before?
questions.a: Been relegated — they were bottom of the table in April 2015 before a miraculous survival run

questions.q: The 'Hand of God' is famous — but what happened with Maradona's second goal in that same match that's considered even more remarkable?
questions.a: He dribbled past five England players and the goalkeeper in a 60-metre run — often called the 'Goal of the Century'

questions.q: In Formula 1, only one driver has won the World Championship posthumously. Who?
questions.a: Jochen Rindt in 1970 — he died at Monza with a points lead that nobody overtook

questions.q: What is 'rotating the strike' in cricket and why is it tactically important?
questions.a: Batters taking singles to swap ends, ensuring the stronger batter faces the weaker bowler and keeping the scoreboard ticking between boundaries
